metadata.name: Ohlone corpus source backlog
metadata.purpose: High-value sources to evaluate before adding more dictionary, text, or audio material.
metadata.review_policy: Prefer primary archives, published dictionaries/grammars, and community-approved resources. Separate discovery from reuse rights.

items.name: Mutsun-English English-Mutsun Dictionary PDF
items.why_it_matters: This is a 677-page text-readable dictionary with CC BY-NC 4.0 licensing and enough structure to become the primary Mutsun lexical source.
items.next_action: Parse the scraped page/chunk files into reviewed dictionary entries and examples.

items.name: Mutsun Text Collection
items.why_it_matters: Longer texts are more valuable than isolated word lists for grammar, examples, and RAG context.
items.next_action: Inventory each downloadable text and map it to phrase/example records with page or item references.

items.name: Quizlet: Chochenyo final set (all words)
items.why_it_matters: Search indexing reports a 188-card Chochenyo learning set with greetings, pronouns, and everyday vocabulary, which could help identify modern learner forms to verify against primary/community sources.
items.next_action: Do not bulk scrape. Ask the set author or relevant Chochenyo/Muwekma language authority for permission, then verify every card against primary or community-approved sources before ingestion.

items.name: Mutsun Language Database Exports
items.why_it_matters: Potentially structured lexical and text material that may reduce manual cleanup.
items.next_action: Check download access, license, and field schema before import.

items.name: Pinart mission vocabularies / Heizer 1952
items.why_it_matters: Digitized mission-era Costanoan wordlists may fill gaps for Chalon, Awaswas, Rumsen, and related historical varieties.
items.next_action: Review edition rights and community sensitivity, then extract item-level vocabulary with historical-transcription status.

items.name: Schoolcraft Costanos vocabulary
items.why_it_matters: One of the few online lexical leads for the Mission Dolores / San Francisco Bay area vocabulary.
items.next_action: Extract only after Ramaytush review; label forms as early colonial transcription.

items.name: Powell 1877 Tribes of California appendix
items.why_it_matters: Public-domain comparative lists may add Tamyen and Santa Clara evidence where the current corpus is thin.
items.next_action: Use as historical evidence only, with exact source labels and no automatic normalization.

items.name: Henshaw mission vocabularies / Heizer 1955
items.why_it_matters: Companion mission vocabulary source that may explain or validate Rumsen and other Costanoan forms.
items.next_action: Review edition rights and compare against primary transcriptions before ingestion.

items.name: California Language Archive - Chochenyo
items.why_it_matters: Primary catalog for recordings, field notes, and collection metadata.
items.next_action: Create item-level records for publicly viewable materials and restricted-access requests.

items.name: California Language Archive - Mutsun
items.why_it_matters: Primary archive path for legacy Mutsun recordings and manuscripts.
items.next_action: Cross-reference CLA item identifiers with current audio and source tables.

items.name: Smithsonian Harrington Costanoan Papers
items.why_it_matters: Field notes are central evidence for many varieties but require careful transcription and provenance.
items.next_action: Build an item-level finding-aid index and mark which boxes/folders contain language data.

items.name: ASJP Rumsen wordlist
items.why_it_matters: Small normalized 40-item comparative list useful for computational comparison and sanity checks.
items.next_action: Use as secondary comparison data only; verify every form against primary/community sources.

items.name: Kroeber 1910: The Chumash and Costanoan Languages
items.why_it_matters: Public-domain comparative forms and classification notes can support source interpretation across Costanoan varieties.
items.next_action: Use for bibliography and cross-checks; do not treat comparative forms as community vocabulary.

items.name: Kroeber 1904: Languages of the Coast of California South of San Francisco
items.why_it_matters: Early southern Costanoan analysis may help with Rumsen and Monterey-area historical forms.
items.next_action: Ingest selectively, marking all forms as historical transcription.

items.name: Mason 1916: The Mutsun Dialect of Costanoan
items.why_it_matters: Useful public-domain cross-check for Arroyo/Okrand/Warner-derived Mutsun data.
items.next_action: Use primarily for validation against stronger Mutsun sources already in the corpus.

items.name: Beeler 1972: An Extension of San Francisco Bay Costanoan?
items.why_it_matters: Helps interpret San Francisco Bay Costanoan classification and the Schoolcraft/Alcantara vocabulary.
items.next_action: Use as citation and analysis only, not as bulk lexical data.

items.name: Levy 1976: Costanoan Internal Relationships
items.why_it_matters: Useful bibliography and dialect relationship layer for interpreting source-of-sources evidence.
items.next_action: Use for source mapping and validation, not direct dictionary data.

items.name: Ohlone Spoken Word audio
items.why_it_matters: A public audio lead that may contain useful spoken examples if rights and transcription are clear.
items.next_action: Verify license, speaker consent, and transcript availability before creating audio segments.

items.name: Muwekma Ohlone Language Revitalization
items.why_it_matters: Community context should frame Chochenyo data use and attribution.
items.next_action: Keep as citation/context unless explicit downloadable language data is offered.

items.name: Muwekma Ohlone educational toolkit
items.why_it_matters: Community-framed educational material can guide context, naming, and respectful source presentation.
items.next_action: Link and cite; do not bulk ingest Chochenyo language content without Muwekma permission.

items.name: mak-'amham / Cafe Ohlone
items.why_it_matters: Modern public Ohlone language use in cultural context can identify living-language usage and orthographic choices.
items.next_action: Treat as living community intellectual property; metadata only unless explicit permission is granted.

items.name: Ramaytush Ohlone terminology
items.why_it_matters: Important rights and naming guidance before any Ramaytush lexical ingestion.
items.next_action: Use to shape permission workflow and citation language.

items.name: SFPUC Ohlone language article
items.why_it_matters: A public lead for Ramaytush language visibility, including plaque vocabulary references.
items.next_action: Verify provenance and permission before extracting any plaque words.

items.name: Amah Mutsun Language
items.why_it_matters: Community context should frame Mutsun data use and attribution.
items.next_action: Keep as citation/context unless explicit downloadable language data is offered.

items.name: Sogorea Te' / Mak Noono Tiirinikma
items.why_it_matters: Community-led learning materials can clarify current usage and spelling choices.
items.next_action: Do not scrape beyond public citation without permission.

items.name: UC Davis Harrington Database Project
items.why_it_matters: May help locate Harrington items and metadata across institutions.
items.next_action: Use as a discovery index, not as lexical evidence unless item-level text is available.
